units.mitra: The subject matter for today: 1. Reflecting on death and impermanence. Regarding impermanence, there are two types: coarse impermanence and subtle impermanence. The second, subtle impermanence, is the moment-by-moment transformation of phenomena. The method for meditating on one’s own death and impermanence consists of three techniques. Meditating on the certainty of one’s own death.

text: Meditating that the time of death is uncertain.
Meditating that at death nothing but the Dharma will help.
The world's variety comes from karma.
For example, even the outer world, the environment, comes from karma as its cause.

notes.text: Treasury of Abhidharma (chos mngon pa'i mdzod kyi tshig le'ur byas pa, Vasubandhu), Toh 4089, 10b-43, opening line of ch. 4: las las 'jig rten sna tshogs skyes; the notes quote it from memory as 'jig rten sna tshogs las las grub (order inverted, grub for skyes), translated as given (dm_identify_U02.txt, dm_identify_U02-2.txt, dm_cite_U02.txt). Register row P01/U02; TITLE row fixed.

the Treasury's own commentary (Bhāṣya, Toh 4090, 166a-3–7; the same in Toh 4091, 157a-11–15, and Toh 4095, 143a-21–24) reads 'jig rten sna tshogs as the many varieties of the world of beings and of the container world (sems can dang snod kyi 'jig rten), made by no one with prior intent and arising from the karma of beings; Gendun Drup (ACIP SL5525N_T:6430): las las snod bcud kyi 'jig rten sna tshogs pa skyes so. Followed: "the world's variety"; it also settles the example.

rgyu las las grub: resolved by the Bhāṣya and KHEZ022:9760 (snod bcud kyi 'jig rten … rgyu gang las byung … las las): karma is the cause even of the container world, "comes from karma as its cause", taken; the alternative (a dittography for rgyu las grub, "comes from causes", cf. dang dang in U01) has no support.
phyi snod 'jig rten yang "the outer world, the environment, also / too" (MITRA "also"); "even" taken for the point the commentaries make (not only beings but their world).
'khor ba sdug bsngal bsam pa "Contemplating that samsara is suffering".

snod (container) image let go: "the environment" (snod bcud = environment and inhabitants). Frame mngon pa mdzod las … gsungs pa ltar → "As the Treasury of Abhidharma says:" (block form of the inline formula; keeps ltar). The 7-syllable line set as a one-line verse block; beats.py with "variety" hand-counted (va-RI-e-ty, not in its lexicon); "The world in all its variety …" dropped (pulse fail, filler "all").

items 2–3: chos ma gtogs gang gis kyang mi phan in the lamrim works (TSD RDI-TOK-07:2403; Dwags po chos bzhi'i 'grel pa, TSD BEN-LB-017:704: chos kho na bya dgos) → chos = the Dharma one practises; "the Dharma" kept.

[nam 'chi] [cha med] (when one dies — no certainty) → content of sgom pa. [shi tshe] [chos ma gtogs] [gang gis] [mi phan] → content of sgom pa ("at death nothing but the Dharma helps"). Quote: ['jig rten sna tshogs] [las las] grub (the varied world is produced from karma). Frame: mngon pa mdzod las … gsungs pa ltar (as the Kośa says). Example: dper na [phyi snod 'jig rten yang] [rgyu las las] grub.

shi tshe = temporal "at death / when one has died"; ma gtogs = exception "except, nothing but"; gang gis … mi = instrument/agent + negation = "nothing (helps)"; par sgom pa = content complement; skor = topic "on, about"; las (after mdzod) = source of the quote; las las = karma + ablative = source "from karma"; gsungs pa ltar = "as (it) says" (manner, links the quote to the example); dper na = "for example"; yang = "even / also"; rgyu las las = "from karma as its cause".
mi phan (negated, scope: gang gis = nothing at all helps); ma gtogs (exception); cha med (negated existential: no certainty); yang (even). No numbers.

nam 'chi cha med = the time of death is uncertain; chos = the Dharma; las = karma; las 'bras = karma and its results; 'jig rten sna tshogs = the world's variety (draft had "the world in all its variety": PULSE fail and filler "all"); las las grub = comes from karma; phyi snod 'jig rten = the outer world, the environment (snod = container: image let go); rgyu = cause; 'khor ba = samsara; sdug bsngal = suffering.

rgyu las las grub: (a) rgyu in apposition to las (karma) + ablative = "comes from karma as its cause", taken (it illustrates the quote, and yang = "even the outer world" needs karma as the point); (b) dittography for rgyu las grub "comes from causes" (cf. dang dang, U01). Ground in the Kośa's own commentary on the line (karma and the receptacle world).
the quotation is not the canonical wording: the Kośa's line (as remembered) is las las 'jig rten sna tshogs skyes; translated as the notes give it (grub); identify.
gsungs (in gsungs pa ltar): agent = the treatise/its author; "as the Treasury … says".

'khor ba sdug bsngal bsam pa: "the suffering of samsara", taken (heading form, parallel to 'chi ba mi rtag pa bsam pa); alt. "that samsara is suffering" (U03's definition reads samsara as by nature suffering).
shi tshe = at death (shi = past stem: "when one has died / at the time of death"); "at death" covers both.

Kośa root verified: Toh 4089, 10b-43 (las las 'jig rten sna tshogs skyes// de ni sems pa dang des byas//), opening line of ch. 4 (Bhāṣya 166a-1 closes ch. 3 just before); the notes paraphrase it ('jig rten sna tshogs las las grub). Gloss (dm_gloss_U02.txt): Bhāṣya Toh 4090, 166a-3–7 (same in Toh 4091, 157a-11–15; Toh 4095, 143a-21–24): yang sems can dang snod kyi 'jig rten rnam pa mang po sna tshogs pa … de sus byas she na/ sus kyang blo sngon du btang ste byas pa ni med do// … sems can rnams kyi/ las las 'jig rten sna tshogs skyes = the variety of the world of beings AND of the container world was made by no one with prior intent; it arises from the karma of beings. Gendun Drup (ACIP SL5525N_T:6430): las las snod bcud kyi 'jig rten sna tshogs pa skyes so; KHEZ022:9760: snod bcud kyi 'jig rten … rgyu gang las byung … las las. → resolves the Q on rgyu las las grub: branch (a), karma is the cause even of the container world; followed (body as drafted). Death items: chos ma gtogs gang gis kyang mi phan (RDI-TOK-07:2403; Dwags po chos bzhi'i 'grel pa, TSD BEN-LB-017:704: chos kho na bya dgos) → chos = the Dharma one practises; body unchanged.

units.mitra: Meditate on the uncertainty of the time of death. Meditate on the fact that at the time of death, nothing is of benefit except the Dharma. Regarding karma and its results: as stated in the *Abhidharmakośa*, "The variety of the world is formed from karma." For example, the external vessel-world also arises from the cause of karma. Contemplate the suffering of cyclic existence.

text: Once you recognize that samsara is by nature the three kinds of suffering, the wish to be free from it arises. This is what the teachings call renunciation.

footnotes.text: Pain is the suffering of suffering, passing pleasure is the suffering of change, and the suffering of conditioning is called pervasive because it runs through every feeling, even the neutral ones.

construal.text: prose: one definitional period (3 clauses, ~37 syllables), then a heading and a three-item list. Register: exposition (definition), plain.

(elided agent: the practitioner) shes par byed ['khor ba de … rang bzhin du] → nas → [de las thar 'dod kyi blo] skye ba → la → (elided honorific agent: the Buddha/masters/the teacher) gsungs kyis yod [nges 'byung] = "X arising is what (they) call renunciation".

'khor ba de = samsara (de resumes U02's closing heading); gsum gyi rang bzhin du = "as having the nature of the three sufferings" (adverbial of the knowing); nas = sequence: having recognized → then the wish arises (keep the order; not upgraded to cause); de las = source "from it (samsara)"; thar 'dod kyi blo = attitude of wanting to be free; skye ba la … gsungs = naming: "(the arising) is called"; gsungs kyis yod = gsung gi yod, colloquial present-habitual honorific "(they) say/call".
gsum (three) twice. No negation.

'khor ba = samsara; sdug bsngal gsum = the three kinds of suffering; rang bzhin = nature ("by nature"); thar 'dod kyi blo = the wish to be free; nges 'byung = renunciation; sdug bsngal gyi sdug bsngal = the suffering of suffering; 'gyur ba'i sdug bsngal = the suffering of change; khyab pa 'du byed kyi sdug bsngal = the pervasive suffering of conditioning.
agent of shes par byed: the practitioner, generic → "you" (lesson register); alt. impersonal ("recognizing samsara as …").
agent of gsungs: the Buddha / the masters / the class's teacher (lesson notes); rendered "what the teachings call" (honorific realized by register, no person invented); alt. passive "is called".
nges 'byungs = nges 'byung (final s a slip); gsungs kyis = gsung gi (colloquial auxiliary).
khyab pa = "pervasive" (not kun khyab "all-pervasive"); bound term "the pervasive suffering of conditioning"; Alt: "all-pervasive suffering of conditioned existence".

Toh 3996 (rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba dang po dang rnam par 'byed pa bstan pa'i … bshad pa), 165a-18–26: sdug bsngal ni sdug bsngal ba'i sdug bsngal nyid … bde ba ni 'gyur ba'i sdug bsngal nyid … sdug bsngal yang ma yin bde ba yang ma yin pa ni 'du byed kyi sdug bsngal nyid … de khyab pa yin pa'i phyir ro zhes bya ba ni 'du byed kyi sdug bsngal la bya ste/ de ni tshor ba thams cad la khyab pas so = pain / pleasure / neither; "pervasive" because it pervades every feeling. Toh 4421, 194a-19–194b-8: same by feeling type (pleasant things: grief when parted from them; the rest: conditioned by causes and conditions). zhal gdams lam rim ye shes snying po'i rnam 'grel rab gsal nyin byed (TSD KN-LYN-02:1476–1490): the three; samsaric happiness mi rtag g.yo ba; then 'khor ba'i gnas gang du skyes kyang sdug bsngal gsum gyi rang bzhin las ma 'das pas de dag las myur du thar bar 'dod pa'i blo … bskyed par bya = the same move as U03's definition (samsara by nature the three sufferings → the wish to be free). Terms and reading confirmed; footnote on the three written from 3996/4421/KN-LYN-02. MITRA: agrees (same three terms; gsungs as "is taught as").

units.mitra: Having realized that samsara is of the nature of the three sufferings, the arising of the mind that wishes to be liberated from it is taught as renunciation. The three sufferings are: the suffering of suffering, the suffering of change, and the pervasive suffering of conditioning.
